subject.title: PR2/5 durable core: runtime foundation and terminal immutability guard

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this new shared durable-runtime, schema, Gateway, and environment contract on the 2026.7.1 release line, or should durable guarantees be evolved through the existing task, subagent, session, and delivery owners?
rationale: The patch creates a broad new core persistence and protocol boundary; correctness fixes alone cannot decide whether that permanent architecture belongs in the release line.

options.title: Sponsor and narrow the architecture
options.body: Approve the durable-core direction, then require a current-owner-boundary rebase, blocking fixes, and complete upgrade/live proof before merge.

options.title: Accept as a release experiment
options.body: Intentionally accept the new opt-in release-line contracts after the concrete defects are fixed and exact-head upgrade and runtime evidence is attached.

options.title: Keep existing runtime owners
options.body: Decline the parallel durable layer and pursue narrower durability improvements in the existing task, subagent, session, and delivery stores.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and narrow the architecture
recommendation.body: Approve the durable-core direction, then require a current-owner-boundary rebase, blocking fixes, and complete upgrade/live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a release-line core architecture and product-boundary decision spanning shared state, Gateway protocol, agents, and operator surfaces.
